summary: Entity links no longer slow a long chat while an answer streams, and a matcher chip follows its text when a chunk or new matchers change the hit under it.
howTo: Nothing to do. What an app can notice: a custom components.MentionChip in a finished message is no longer unmounted and mounted again per streamed chunk (its state and effects stay), and useChatEntityLinks().markdownComponents keep one identity for the provider's lifetime. A matcher chip whose hit changes (MAR-5 to MAR-51) shows the new record, also in EntityText, where 0.29.0 kept the old one. Apps that change messages in place (not the AI SDK) should replace a changed output, input or result object rather than mutate it: changes inside the same object are not noticed. A custom Markdown renderer gets the full effect only when it passes markdownComponents (or stable components of its own) to react-markdown.
